meta.title: Download · Aethyr
meta.description: Download the Aethyr plugin for Unreal Engine 5. The Unreal modules come as source for UE 5.8 and later, and the MCP server comes precompiled.

article.heading: Summon Aethyr.
article.lead: Two zips, one plugin. Both carry the MCP server already compiled. The difference is whether the Unreal modules come as source, ready to build against your engine, or prebuilt for UE 5.8.

sections.heading: Let your AI install it
sections.html:
Open your AI assistant in your Unreal project and say "get Aethyr from aethyr.gg". It reads aethyr.gg/install.md, a step-by-step playbook written for AI assistants, and follows it:

  1. It finds your .uproject and downloads the install script into your project's Saved folder.
  2. It runs a preview and shows you what would change: the plugin files, your MCP client config, the bundled skills.
  3. It asks once. After your yes it installs, then tells you what's left, like restarting the editor.

It never runs Perforce commands. Files that are read-only get made writable, and you reconcile them in P4V afterward.

On Fab? A Fab install updates through Fab, and this setup refuses to replace it.

sections.heading: Install with the script
sections.html:
The script your AI runs is aethyr.gg/install.ps1, and you can run it yourself. Open PowerShell in your project folder:

  1. Get it. Invoke-WebRequest https://aethyr.gg/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1, then read it.
  2. Preview. powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1 -DryRun downloads and checks the release and lists every change without making one.
  3. Install. The same command without -DryRun.
  4. Check it. .\Plugins\Aethyr\Binaries\Win64\AethyrMcp.exe doctor should end with Result: OK. Then restart your AI client.

It needs no admin rights. It writes inside the project, plus the MCP client config files it lists (some live in your user profile). -Project <folder> points it at a project other than the current folder.

sections.heading: Get the plugin
sections.html:
◈ Any UE 5.8+ engineAethyr pluginUE 5.8+modules as sourceserver precompiled↓DownloadAethyr-plugin.zip◈ Drop-in for UE 5.8Aethyr plugin, precompiledUE 5.8no build stepserver precompiled↓DownloadAethyr-plugin-precompiled.zip

Every release lives at aethyrgames/aethyr-mcp-releases on GitHub.

sections.heading: Which zip?
sections.html:
• On UE 5.8 installed from the Epic Games Launcher? Take the precompiled zip. Unzip it and launch the editor, nothing to build.
  • On a custom or source-built engine, even one that says 5.8? Take Aethyr-plugin.zip. Precompiled modules only load on the exact engine build they were compiled for, so a custom engine needs the source zip built against it. A quick way to tell: a Launcher engine has Engine/Build/InstalledBuild.txt, a custom one doesn't.
  • On another engine version, or you'd rather build it yourself? Take Aethyr-plugin.zip. The Unreal modules come as C++ source and compile against your engine.

Aethyr needs UE 5.8 or later. Setup checks the engine version itself.

sections.heading: What's in the zip
sections.html:
• Source/AethyrEditor and Source/AethyrRuntime: the two Unreal modules, as C++ source.
  • Binaries/Win64/AethyrMcp.exe: the MCP server. It doesn't link against the engine, which lets one build cover every engine version.
  • Claude/: skills and an audit agent that teach your AI assistant to use the tools well.
  • SETUP.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and README.md: setup and usage guides, written so an AI assistant can follow them.
  • NOTICE.md: third-party notices.

The precompiled zip keeps the source and adds the built module DLLs, plus UnrealEditor.modules and aethyr-precompiled.json, which record the engine build they were compiled for.

sections.heading: Install by hand
sections.html:
1. Download a zip from Get the plugin and the release's SHA256SUMS, and check the hash.
  2. Unblock and unzip it into your project's Plugins folder. Unblock-File clears the downloaded-from-the-internet mark first. You should end up with Plugins/Aethyr/Aethyr.uplugin.
  3. Source zip only: build the modules (Build for your engine). In a C++ project you can also open the project and let the editor rebuild them when it asks.
  4. Connect your AI client. For Claude Code, Copilot CLI and VS Code Copilot, put this in .mcp.json in the project folder. It holds no absolute path, so it's safe to commit:
    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "aethyr": {
      "command": "./Plugins/Aethyr/Binaries/Win64/AethyrMcp.exe",
      "args": ["--serve-installed-project"]
    }
  }
}
    Other clients take the same entry in their own config file. See Connect your AI.
  5. Check it. .\Plugins\Aethyr\Binaries\Win64\AethyrMcp.exe doctor should end with Result: OK. Restart your AI client and the editor.
  6. Credit. Aethyr is free to use. If you ship something made with it, credit Doug Fessler, for example "Aethyr by Doug Fessler (https://aethyr.gg)". See License.

A hand install skips what setup adds on top: the bundled skills and agent, and the Claude Code permission that lets Aethyr's tools run without a prompt. Run AethyrMcp.exe setup any time to add them.

Writes are on in this build. Every write tool works out of the box. Set AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1 in the server's environment for a session that can only read.

Engine not found? If AethyrMcp.exe doctor reports "engine directory not configured", set AETHYR_ENGINE_DIR to your engine root, like C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8. Aethyr 0.1.1 and older only find engines registered by a source build, not Launcher installs.

sections.heading: Build for your engine
sections.html:
This compiles the plugin against the engine you run it from. You'll need that engine and Visual Studio's C++ build tools.

"<Engine>\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat" BuildPlugin -Plugin="<Unzipped>\Aethyr\Aethyr.uplugin" -Package="C:\AethyrBuild" -TargetPlatforms=Win64

The package folder gets the built modules without the server exe or the docs. Copy its binaries into the plugin you unzipped:

robocopy "C:\AethyrBuild\Binaries" "<YourProject>\Plugins\Aethyr\Binaries" /E /XF *.pdb

Keep the package path short. Unreal Build Tool fails without printing a compiler error once an intermediate file path passes 260 characters. A folder like C:\AethyrBuild stays well under that.

sections.heading: Check the download
sections.html:
Every release carries a SHA256SUMS file. Hash your download in PowerShell:

Get-FileHash .\Aethyr-plugin.zip -Algorithm SHA256

The hash should match that file's line in SHA256SUMS. Case doesn't matter. Older versions are on the releases page.

sections.heading: Updating
sections.html:
1. Ask your assistant. Say "update Aethyr". If Aethyr's tools respond, it previews with apply_update, asks you, and applies it. If they don't, it runs the same setup as a first install, which detects the existing install and updates it.
  2. Or run the script. install.ps1 updates an existing install the same way it installs a new one.
  3. Or do it by hand. Close the editor and your MCP client, download the new zip, and replace the Plugins/Aethyr folder with its contents. Delete Plugins/Aethyr/Intermediate first, so stale generated files can't break the build. Source zip users rebuild afterward.

After an update, restart your MCP client and the editor. health_check reports the new version. Fab installs update through Fab.

sections.heading: Uninstall with your AI
sections.html: Say "uninstall Aethyr". Your AI follows the uninstall steps in install.md: it previews the removal, shows you everything it will change, asks once, removes it, and checks the plugin folder is gone. It never closes your editor for you. If the editor is open on the project, it asks you to close it first.

sections.heading: Uninstall with the script
sections.html:
The plugin carries its own uninstaller. In PowerShell, in your project folder, close the editor and your AI client first:

  1. Preview. .\Plugins\Aethyr\Binaries\Win64\AethyrMcp.exe uninstall --dry-run lists every change and makes none.
  2. Remove it. The same command without --dry-run. The plugin folder goes a moment after the command exits, since a running program can't delete its own folder.

It removes what setup wrote and nothing else: the aethyr entry in your MCP client configs, the Aethyr skills and agent, Aethyr's permission in Claude Code's settings, Saved/Aethyr and Plugins/Aethyr. A skill you edited is kept and listed. Your other MCP servers and skills, the .uproject, your source and your engine aren't touched. It never runs Perforce commands. --keep-plugin leaves the plugin folder in place.

Shared settings. The Claude Code permission and the guidance in your user profile serve every project on the machine. If another project still uses Aethyr, run setup there to put them back.

sections.heading: Uninstall by hand
sections.html:
For a hand install, close the editor and your AI client, then:

  1. Delete Plugins/Aethyr.
  2. Remove the aethyr entry from .mcp.json, or delete the file if that was all it held.

If you installed with setup, it also wrote these. Delete the ones you find:

  • Saved/Aethyr in the project.
  • The aethyr-* folders under .claude/skills, aethyr-bp-audit.md under .claude/agents and .github/agents, and each aethyr-managed-assets.json beside them.
  • "mcp__aethyr" in permissions.allow and "aethyr" in enabledMcpjsonServers in ~/.claude/settings.json.
  • The aethyr entry in any user-scope client config, and the section between aethyr:start and aethyr:end in ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md.
  • Aethyr's section in Config/DefaultAethyr.ini, if you used --deny.

The script does all of that for you, and only what setup wrote.
